reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses general magnetocaloric figures of merit and annealing effects in bulk HEAs, but provides no specific support for the key premises about nanoscale strain-induced domain-wall pinning, heat-transfer limitations in thin films, or the effects of low-temperature annealing on defect density and domain-wall mobility in the proposed FeMnNiGeSi system.
premises: Deposition-induced lattice strain and compositional fluctuations pin magnetic domain walls in as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi thin films/nanoribbons.
Domain-wall pinning broadens the entropy change profile and increases hysteresis compared to bulk forms.
Low-dimensional architectures have intrinsically limited heat-transfer capacity that restricts cycle frequency.
Low-temperature annealing partially relieves lattice strain and reduces defect density without causing grain coarsening or phase transformation.
Reduced pinning from annealing leads to more mobile domain walls, sharpening the entropy change profile and reducing hysteresis.
